title: Silky sweet potato puree
summary: Naturally sweet, bright orange and freezer-friendly: one of the easiest first foods there is.
texture: Completely smooth and spoonable, like thick yogurt. Thin with breast milk, formula or water a teaspoon at a time. As baby gets used to it, mash with a fork instead of blending to make it slightly thicker.
ingredients: Breast milk, prepared infant formula or water, to thin
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Wash the sweet potato and prick it all over with a fork.
Bake on a lined tray for 40 to 50 minutes, until a knife slides into the middle with no resistance.
Let it cool, then split it open and scoop the flesh into a blender or bowl. Discard the skin.
Blend or mash until smooth, adding liquid a little at a time until it drops easily off a spoon.
choking: Blend until there are no fibrous strands or firm pieces left.
Remove every bit of skin: it doesn't break down and can stick in baby's mouth.
storage: Fridge up to 2 days in a sealed container, or freeze in an ice-cube tray, then bag the cubes, up to 1 month. Thaw in the fridge and warm gently. Stir and check the temperature before serving.
tips: Steaming works too: peel, cube and steam for 12 to 15 minutes until very soft.
Mix a cube with lentil or meat puree later on for an iron boost.
